title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: The Federation of Chambers of Industry and its members represent Syria’s industrial private sector within a historically constrained institutional environment marked by limited capacity and restricted autonomy. Under the former regime, governance processes lacked competition, with leadership closely linked to political networks, reducing the Chambers’ ability to deliver technical services and effective advocacy. Recent assessments indicate a strong willingness of the private sector to contribute to the economic revitalization of the country, but this is hindered by an unconducive business environment and a reduced membership base within the Industrial Chambers, which weakens their capacity to represent businesses effectively. The Chambers are also understaffed and have limited technical expertise. Despite these challenges, the Chambers remain important actors for industrial resilience and recovery. Key sectors—including textiles and garments, agro-processing, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, and construction materials—have been severely affected by conflict, displacement, infrastructure damage, and sanctions. There is a need to develop a joint advocacy strategy and position paper identifying priority challenges and reforms to support economic recovery, while strengthening the Federation’s role and capacity to engage government on policy reforms, as well as the capacity of regional chambers to contribute to these efforts and provide improved services to their members.
